predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: 'The new state only controlled the northern Chahar province initially' (Suiyuan campaign page); Chahar had been occupied 'starting in 1933' by Manchukuo and Japanese armies (Mengjiang page)

successors.name: Republic of China
successors.text: 'The territory returned to Chinese control after the defeat of the Japanese Empire in 1945'; 'Most of the area, with the notable exception of Kalgan, is now part of Inner Mongolia'

rulers.name: Yondonwangchug (Prince of Ulanqab)
rulers.title: first chairman of the Mongol Military Government

ledger.x: 1936: Demchugdongrub's Mongol Military Government is formed under Japanese patronage.
12 May 1936: the Mongol Military Government is Japan's client from its foundation.
1937: eastern Suiyuan falls to the Inner Mongols and the Japanese.
1937: eastern Suiyuan joins the same client state with its gain.
8 August 1937: Operation Chahar begins.

17 October 1937: Operation Chahar ends in a 'Japanese victory'; on 4 September a Japanese-aligned South Chahar Government was set up at Kalgan and Chahar's 'complete independence' was declared by 'one hundred influential persons' headed by Demchugdongrub.
October 1937: the Mongol Military Government is renamed the Mongol United Autonomous Government.
1 September 1939: the South Chahar government merges into the Mongol United Autonomous Government.
1 September 1939: the North Shanxi government joins the merger (see the South Chahar event).

1 September 1939: South Chahar and North Shanxi join the same client state in the merger ('formed in 1939 as its own puppet state of the Empire of Japan', infobox status 'Puppet state of the Empire of Japan (1939-40)').
1 September 1939: the merged state is the Mengjiang of the Wikipedia article; the page says it was 'formed in 1939 as its own puppet state of the Empire of Japan'.
24 March 1940: Mengjiang is incorporated into the Reorganized National Government (Wang Jingwei regime).
4 August 1941: the state is renamed again.
August 1945: Soviet and Mongolian cavalry enter Inner Mongolia.
19 August 1945: Mengjiang capitulates.
19 August 1945: the client relation ends with the state.
19 August 1945: the client relation ends with the state.
19 August 1945: the client relation ends with the state.
19 August 1945: the client relation ends with the state.
19 August 1945: Mengjiang is disestablished.

wars.name: Suiyuan campaign
wars.outcome: Chinese victory: Fu Zuoyi's 35th Army beat Demchugdongrub's Inner Mongolian Army and Wang Ying's Grand Han Righteous Army, with Japanese advisers and air support, at Hongort (14-16 November) and Bailingmiao (from 17 November 1936); Suiyuan stayed Chinese…

wars.name: Operation Chahar
wars.outcome: Japanese victory: Kalgan fell on 27 August 1937 and Xuanhua was reached by 7 September; the operation ended on 17 October 1937.

wars.name: Battle of Taiyuan
wars.outcome: Japanese victory: 'part of Suiyuan, most of Shanxi and the NRA arsenal at Taiyuan'; the 9th Mongolian cavalry division and the Mongol Military Government fought on the Japanese side.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria (Inner Mongolia front)
wars.outcome: Soviet victory; Mengjiang collapsed and its land went back to Chinese control.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary: the north Chahar and eastern Suiyuan shapes are rings and radii, and the line against Chinese-held Suiyuan was a front that moved with the war.
